description: tt marks a written T by the original token at the head of its own span. In the check, c reads the synthetic T and then F through #, so the head of tt is F, tt has no ~written, and c is no reading. The check passes. Compare reparse-written-observation-text (engine §7.4, §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a A [T] f
%rule b A [T] [T] f
%rule c A $t(tt)
%conditions ~written ⊆ tags($t)
%rule tt [T #] <T ⊆ tags(head($)) ⟹ ~written>
%rule # [F ...]
%rule f F
